# GitHub authority: who may do what, and with which credential

## Current policy

A connected person's code turn holds their GitHub user token and uses `gh`
and HTTPS git directly. Repository instructions determine the publication
workflow, including shared-main pushes; GitHub permissions and rulesets bound
the credential. The dedicated PR MCP tools and the interactive blanket
merge/default-branch prohibition have been removed.

Ask runs, unattended runs, and machine-authored turns keep their App-token
limits and publication guards. Run-scoped `GH_CONFIG_DIR`, bot commit authorship,
`Co-authored-by` attribution, and audit error handling remain unchanged.

The App grant and every installation-token mint exclude repository
Administration. New repository creation happens in the person's GitHub
browser session at `https://github.com/new`; Open Session only connects the
resulting remote. There is no elevated repository-create token or API path.
Connected-user tokens inherit the intersection of the App's permissions and
the person's access, not the installation mint sets. Keeping Administration
out of the App grant therefore matters for interactive runs too.

If an existing App was granted Administration for the previous automatic
creation flow, its owner must remove that permission on GitHub. A code
update cannot reduce an already installed App's grant. Host credential
isolation remains a separate concern (see "Host hygiene").

The credential rollback shipped in `773380904`; this change completes the
interactive tooling/policy rollback of `a8ee01aeee`. See
[GitHub setup](setup/github.md) and [the security model](security-model.md)
for current behavior.

## Historical design

The remaining sections record the superseded design and its rationale, not
current instructions for agents.

Status: Phase 1 (credentials, tools, policy) implemented 2026-09-08; Phase 0
(rulesets, App permission, credential revocation) is operator work per
deployment, and Phases 2 and 3 are open. Written after the credential split
(#318, #319, #325) made the merge button unusable on split-credential
deployments. It replaces the ad-hoc rules that accumulated across
`security-model.md` and `setup/github.md` with one model. Instance-specific
findings that motivated it live in the operator's private notes, not here.
The owner-identity tools shipped as the `opensession-pull-requests` server
(`open_pull_request`, `edit_pull_request`, `propose_merge`); `propose_merge`
posts a notice and the person merges from the PR panel, which is the one-tap
card until a dedicated card lands in the clients.

## The requirement

1. A human who explicitly triggers an action in Open Session acts with their
   full GitHub permissions. Merge, close, review, push: whatever they could do
   on github.com, they can do from the OS UI, attributed to them. A pull
   request the agent opens at the owner's request shows up under the owner's
   name, and "merge this" from the owner is one tap away.
2. No agent process, in any kind of turn, ever holds a credential that can
   merge a pull request, update a protected branch, or approve a review. An
   unattended run, whether an automation, a `github-*` loop, a review, or a
   fix-round handoff into someone's session, can never do those things no
   matter what it finds on the host or what its prompt is told, and neither
   can an agent in the owner's own session.

These are two different principals with two different ceilings. The current
system gives them one ceiling and has been moving it up and down. The line
that matters is not "human versus agent"; it is "a human clicked" versus "a
model decided". Only the first ever reaches `main`.

## How a split-credential deployment fails today

A split-credential deployment caps the App installation at `contents: read`
and hands pushes to a separate git-transport token. Each part is locally
sound and the combination fails both requirements.

### The merge button

`POST /api/sessions/:id/pr-merge` runs `gh pr merge` with the signed-in
human's App user token (`githubMutationCredential`). A GitHub App user token
can never exceed the App's own permissions, and merging needs
`contents: write` as well as `pull_requests: write`. Once the installation is
capped at `contents: read`, every human merge from the UI fails, and the
human falls back to github.com. `audited()` records each failure as
`ok: true`, because a resolved `{ error }` object counts as success.

The cap was deliberate: `setup/github.md` says the split "makes merging
something no credential on the host can do alone". That is requirement 2
applied to principal 1. The App permission set is the ceiling for humans and
bots at once, so lowering it for bots lowers it for humans.

### Agents on a human's behalf

Interactive runs (`prompt`, `goal`, `create`, `linear`, `slack`, `workflow`)
receive the session owner's App user token as `GH_TOKEN` so that PRs are
authored by the human. Whatever the human may do, the agent may do with that
token. Before the cap this included merging; the cap removed it by removing
it from the human too. GitHub has no narrower delegated form of a user token,
so as long as the token is in the agent's shell the choice is binary: the
agent either holds the human's whole authority or none of it. Where the
human is a ruleset bypass actor, "whole authority" means merging without a
review or a green check. A command policy in front of the shell can ask
before `gh pr merge`, but a policy is a check in our code, not in GitHub;
anything it does not recognise goes through as the human. This design takes
the token out of the shell instead. The agent gets the owner's identity only
through tools the gateway executes on the server, and those tools do not
include merge.

A related live bug: `agents/github/handoff.ts` delivers fix-round handoffs
with sender `"GitHub"`. `githubCredentialUser` (#322) treats only the
auto-continue sender as synthetic, so `"GitHub"` shadows the session owner and
the turn runs with an empty token. Michiel and John have already decided that
fix-round replies should post as the bot, not the human. That is the
Automation principal below: a turn that no human started gets an
installation token whatever the sender string says, so the shadowing class
of bug disappears.

### Unattended runs

Ordinary automations are credential-free by design. A run with no injected
credential also gets no `git@github.com` to HTTPS rewrite and no isolated
`gh` config, so `git push` and `gh` fall through to whatever ambient
Shell cwd was reset to /Users/ashish/code/AgentForge

# Worktrees and disk

By default, a code workspace gets an isolated **git worktree**: a separate
working directory and index that shares the registered repository's object
database. Sessions in the same workspace can deliberately share its worktree;
a stacked session gets another branch and worktree. Unrelated branches do not
see each other's edits or contend over one index, and no second clone is needed.

This is also where much of the instance's disk usage goes.

## The shape

On a normal installation using the default worktree root:

```
~/projects/myapp                                  the repository you registered
~/.opensession/worktrees/myapp-fix-login          a code workspace on `fix-login`
~/.opensession/worktrees/myapp-add-metrics        another branch and worktree
~/.opensession/worktrees/myapp-ask-checkout       shared, read-only Ask checkout
```

`paths.worktreesDir` in `~/.opensession/config.json` decides where host
worktrees live. `OPENSESSION_WORKTREES_DIR` overrides it; the normal default is
`~/.opensession/worktrees`. An instance using `OPENSESSION_STATE_DIR` gets a
worktree root inside that state namespace unless either setting overrides it.
Directory names use the repository's configured `wtPrefix` and branch.

A repository started from Open Session itself (Settings → Repositories → New,
or "New repository" in the New session palette's Project picker) is what to
pick for a project that does not exist anywhere yet; a scratch session (Code
with no repo) is only a working directory and never becomes one. The form
asks where it lives:

- **A GitHub owner.** Open Session opens GitHub's new-repository page with the
  owner, name, private visibility and README option prefilled. Check those
  choices and create on GitHub, then return and choose **Connect repository**.
  This clones it to `~/checkouts/<name>` and records its `ghRepo`, so sessions
  have GitHub pull-request support. Personal accounts and organizations both
  work. Grant the App access to the new repository if its installation only
  covers selected repositories. No Administration permission is requested.
- **This server only.** A checkout with a bare origin beside it:

  ```
  ~/checkouts/myapp                                 the checkout sessions branch from
  ~/checkouts/myapp.git                             its origin, a bare repository
  ```

  The server makes the first commit (a README on `main`) and pushes it, so
  the registry sees the same shape as a clone and the first code session gets
  a normal worktree, diff and local review unit. Nothing is published and the
  registry entry has no `ghRepo`, so this choice has no GitHub pull-request
  flow. Changing `origin` and pushing later does **not** update the registered
  GitHub identity or enable PR support. Choose a GitHub organization at
  creation time if you want that integration. Migrating an existing
  server-only registration to GitHub is a separate operator task, not an
  automatic consequence of publishing its commits.

Fresh worktree setup is best-effort. Open Session first tries to seed a ready
warm template, then runs `.agents/setup` or the configured `worktreeSetup`
fallback. It next runs the configured `depsInstall`, or `bun install` when the
worktree root contains `package.json`. A failed setup skips the remaining steps
of that attempt but does not block the session. Interactive creation starts this
work in the background, so the first turn may begin before dependencies finish
installing.

Commit `.agents/setup` and `.agents/portals.json` to let each workspace
provision itself and expose its app as a Portal on demand. This also lets an
agent open its own change in a browser. See [repo-lifecycle.md](repo-lifecycle.md).

## Modes

**`code` sessions** have write access. This is the default. A new code workspace
normally follows its repository setting, while each person can override each
repository under **Preferences** with **Local checkout** or **Separate worktree**.
Additional sessions in an existing workspace keep its worktree, and
a deliberately selected branch or pull request stays isolated. A new branch
starts from the freshly fetched `origin/<defaultBranch>`, including when that
default branch is explicitly selected as a base. The registered checkout stays
fetch-only: its local branch and uncommitted edits are not moved. If no remote
default branch exists, a local default branch can still be used. Explicit feature
bases retain local commits that origin lacks, so sessions can stack on unpushed
work. Worktree sessions can commit and use the repository's configured
pull-request flow.

**`ask` sessions** are read-only. For an isolated repository they share one
per-repo detached checkout (`<wtPrefix>-ask-checkout`) pinned to
`origin/<defaultBranch>`. Open Session refreshes an existing Ask checkout at
most every five minutes. A shared-checkout repository uses its main checkout
instead. Repo-less Ask sessions use a non-git scratch directory.

**Attached repos.** A code session can attach additional repositories. Each
gets an isolated worktree using the session's branch name, and may be reused by
another owner of that branch. Ask sessions and remote or volume-backed Sandbox
workspaces cannot attach repositories. A repository configured as a shared
checkout cannot itself be attached unless shared-checkout behavior has been
disabled.

Sandbox sessions clone inside the Sandbox's own disk and create no host
worktree. Provider-owned cleanup is separate, and destroying a Sandbox deletes
any work not pushed elsewhere. See
[self-hosting-sandboxes.md](self-hosting-sandboxes.md).

## Publication policy

Checkout isolation does not require pull requests. Each repository can set
`publicationMode` in the instance's `~/.opensession/config.json`:

```json
{
  "selfDev": "worktree",
  "repos": {
    "opensession": {
      "repo": "/srv/opensession",
      "sharedCheckout": true,
      "publicationMode": "direct"
    }
  }
}
```

content.text:
I'm assuming you mean [Open Session](https://github.com/tellahq/opensession) (`tellahq/opensession`), an open-source, self-hosted coding-agent orchestrator. Tell me if you meant a different project. I read its docs on GitHub (`docs/worktrees.md`, `docs/self-hosting-sandboxes.md`, `docs/github-authority.md`).

The overall architecture is the same, but the repo handling is different.

**What matches**
- **Agent loop on the server:** only the workspace is remote. In Open Session, `read`, `write`, `edit`, `grep`, `find` and `bash` each become one command in the VM. That is the same as our tools.
- **VM lifecycle:** each session gets its own VM that sleeps when idle and wakes on the next message, with files kept across turns. The idle sleep is 30 minutes by default, against our 1 hour.
- **Provider credentials:** these stay on the server and never go into the VM.

**What differs**

| | Open Session | AgentForge |
|---|---|---|
| Getting the repo into the VM | The VM clones the repo itself, onto its own disk. | The backend downloads a snapshot from GitHub, uploads it, and runs `git init` plus a synthetic base commit. There is no git history. |
| GitHub credentials | Interactive turns receive the user's GitHub token. `git` and `gh` run directly in the session. | No GitHub credential ever enters the VM. The backend publishes through the GitHub API. |
| Surviving a lost VM | After every clean turn it pushes a checkpoint commit of the working tree to a hidden ref on origin. A replaced VM resumes from it. | Nothing is checkpointed. If the VM expires, earlier work is gone and the agent is told. |
| Repo setup | It runs the repo's `.agents/setup` and `.agents/resume` scripts. | We have no equivalent. |
| Local mode | Defaults to a git worktree on the host, and can use a sandbox instead. | Always a sandbox. |

**What this means for us**
- **Size limits:** cloning in the VM would have had no repo size or rate-limit problem, which is the failure you hit. Open Session accepts exposing a token to the agent to get that.
- **Security:** our choice is stricter. Their own history shows the tradeoff: they wrote that a token in the agent's shell is "binary: the agent either holds the human's whole authority or none of it".
- **Gaps:** checkpointing and a setup script are the two features of theirs that would improve ours.

My suggestion is still the signed-link download for private repos, plus a plain clone in the VM for public ones. That keeps our no-credentials rule and removes the size and rate limits. A branch checkpoint like theirs would be a separate improvement.

For `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/tarball/{ref}`, the page documents the following:

- **Status code:** The only documented status is **302 Found**. The response schema for 302 is empty.
- **Location header:** The page doesn't name the header, but it says that if your client doesn't follow redirects, you must "use the Location header to make a second GET request."
- **Link expiration:** For private repositories, the link is temporary. The page says it "expire[s] after five minutes."
- **`ref` parameter:** It's marked required, and the page says that if you omit it, the default branch (usually `main`) is used. It doesn't say whether a commit SHA is accepted.
- **Permissions:** The page doesn't list required permissions, such as contents read.
- **GitHub App user tokens:** The page doesn't say whether they're supported.
- **Rate limits:** The page doesn't mention rate limit implications.

The zipball endpoint (`/zipball/{ref}`) works the same way, with one addition: if the repository is empty, following the redirect returns a 404.

"""Runs INSIDE the sandbox VM, never in the API process: lists and prunes a repository that was just unpacked there.

Standard library only (the VM has Python 3). The API reads this file as text and uploads it (see `vm_repository.py`); tests import
it. Paths are handled as bytes, so a file name that is not valid UTF-8 is listed (as hex) and can still be removed.

  python3 vm_scan.py list <folder> <out.json>   every file, link and special file below <folder>: [{"k": kind, "p": path | "h": hex}]
  python3 vm_scan.py drop <folder> <plan.json>  removes the files a plan names ([{"p": path} | {"h": hex}]); folders are never removed

`kind` is "f" a regular file, "l" a symbolic link (or an extra hard link to a file already listed) and "x" anything else.
"""
import json
import os
import stat
import sys


def scan(root: str) -> list[dict]:
    base = os.fsencode(root)
    found = []
    stack = [b""]
    while stack:
        relative = stack.pop()
        with os.scandir(os.path.join(base, relative) if relative else base) as entries:
            for entry in entries:
                path = os.path.join(relative, entry.name) if relative else entry.name
                info = entry.stat(follow_symlinks=False)
                if stat.S_ISDIR(info.st_mode):
                    stack.append(path)
                    continue
                kind = "l" if stat.S_ISLNK(info.st_mode) else "f" if stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode) else "x"
                found.append((path, kind, info.st_dev, info.st_ino, info.st_nlink))
    found.sort(key=lambda item: item[0])
    linked = set()
    result = []
    for path, kind, device, inode, links in found:
        if kind == "f" and links > 1:
            # A hard link is a second name for a file: the first (in path order) is kept, the others are treated as links.
            if (device, inode) in linked:
                kind = "l"
            else:
                linked.add((device, inode))
        try:
            result.append({"k": kind, "p": path.decode("utf-8")})
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            result.append({"k": kind, "h": path.hex()})
    return result


def drop(root: str, plan: list[dict]) -> int:
    base = os.fsencode(root)
    removed = 0
    for item in plan:
        raw = bytes.fromhex(item["h"]) if "h" in item else item["p"].encode("utf-8")
        parts = raw.split(b"/")
        # A plan can only name something below the folder.
        if not raw or raw.startswith(b"/") or any(part in (b"", b".", b"..") for part in parts):
            continue
        target = os.path.join(base, raw)
        try:
            if os.path.isdir(target) and not os.path.islink(target):
                continue
            os.unlink(target)
            removed += 1
        except FileNotFoundError:
            pass
    return removed


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    if len(argv) != 4 or argv[1] not in ("list", "drop"):
        print("usage: vm_scan.py list|drop <folder> <file>", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    command, root, path = argv[1:]
    if command == "list":
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            json.dump(scan(root), handle)
    else:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            drop(root, json.load(handle))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv))

"""Runs INSIDE the sandbox VM, never in the API process: lists and prunes a repository that was just unpacked there.

Standard library only (the VM has Python 3). The API reads this file as text and uploads it (see `vm_repository.py`); tests import
it. Paths are handled as bytes, so a file name that is not valid UTF-8 is listed (as hex) and can still be removed.

  python3 vm_scan.py list <folder> <out.json>   every file, link and special file below <folder>: [{"k": kind, "p": path | "h": hex}]
  python3 vm_scan.py drop <folder> <plan.json>  removes the files a plan names ([{"p": path} | {"h": hex}]); folders are never removed

`kind` is "f" a regular file, "l" a symbolic link (or an extra hard link to a file already listed) and "x" anything else.
"""
import json
import os
import stat
import sys


def scan(root: str) -> list[dict]:
    base = os.fsencode(root)
    found = []
    stack = [b""]
    while stack:
        relative = stack.pop()
        with os.scandir(os.path.join(base, relative) if relative else base) as entries:
            for entry in entries:
                path = os.path.join(relative, entry.name) if relative else entry.name
                info = entry.stat(follow_symlinks=False)
                if stat.S_ISDIR(info.st_mode):
                    stack.append(path)
                    continue
                kind = "l" if stat.S_ISLNK(info.st_mode) else "f" if stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode) else "x"
                found.append((path, kind, info.st_dev, info.st_ino, info.st_nlink))
    found.sort(key=lambda item: item[0])
    linked = set()
    result = []
    for path, kind, device, inode, links in found:
        if kind == "f" and links > 1:
            # A hard link is a second name for a file: the first (in path order) is kept, the others are treated as links.
            if (device, inode) in linked:
                kind = "l"
            else:
                linked.add((device, inode))
        try:
            result.append({"k": kind, "p": path.decode("utf-8")})
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            result.append({"k": kind, "h": path.hex()})
    return result


def drop(root: str, plan: list[dict]) -> int:
    base = os.fsencode(root)
    removed = 0
    for item in plan:
        raw = bytes.fromhex(item["h"]) if "h" in item else item["p"].encode("utf-8")
        parts = raw.split(b"/")
        # A plan can only name something below the folder.
        if not raw or raw.startswith(b"/") or any(part in (b"", b".", b"..") for part in parts):
            continue
        target = os.path.join(base, raw)
        try:
            if os.path.isdir(target) and not os.path.islink(target):
                continue
            os.unlink(target)
            removed += 1
        except FileNotFoundError:
            pass
    return removed


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    if len(argv) != 4 or argv[1] not in ("list", "drop"):
        print("usage: vm_scan.py list|drop <folder> <file>", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    command, root, path = argv[1:]
    if command == "list":
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            json.dump(scan(root), handle)
    else:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            drop(root, json.load(handle))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv))

"""Loading a repository by letting the sandbox download it: the VM-side scripts run for real (with the paths in a temporary folder),
the plan of what to leave out, the GitHub archive links, and how the load falls back to the snapshot upload."""
import asyncio
import json
import os
import pathlib
import shlex
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from types import SimpleNamespace as NS
from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, patch

import httpx

from agentforge.integrations.e2b_sandbox import SandboxUnavailable
from agentforge.integrations.github_app import AuthorizedGitHubClient, GitHubAppClient
from agentforge.integrations.github_client import ArchiveLink, GitHubClient, GitHubError
from agentforge.sandbox import vm_repository, vm_scan
from agentforge.tools.sandbox_shell import BASE_TAG, MARKER

from test_github_app_client import SHA as APP_SHA, settings as app_settings
from test_sandbox_shell import Env, REPO, SHA

URL = "https://codeload.github.com/owner/repo/legacy.tar.gz/" + SHA + "?token=SECRETTOKEN"


class Folder(unittest.TestCase):
    """A temporary folder standing in for the VM's file system: every path constant of `vm_repository` points into it."""

    def setUp(self):
        self.root = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="repo-download-"))
        self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, self.root, True)
        paths = {"STAGE": self.root / "stage", "SCAN": self.root / "scan.py", "LIST": self.root / "list.json", "DROP": self.root / "drop.json",
                 "CURL_CONFIG": self.root / "curl", "ARCHIVE": self.root / "repo.tgz", "WORKSPACE": self.root / "workspace"}
        patcher = patch.multiple(vm_repository, PYTHON=sys.executable, **{key: str(value) for key, value in paths.items()})
        patcher.start()
        self.addCleanup(patcher.stop)
        patch.object(vm_repository, "LEFTOVERS", tuple(str(paths[name]) for name in ("STAGE", "LIST", "DROP", "CURL_CONFIG", "ARCHIVE", "SCAN"))).start()
        self.addCleanup(patch.stopall)
        self.stage, self.workspace = paths["STAGE"], paths["WORKSPACE"]
        self.workspace.mkdir()

    def put(self, folder: pathlib.Path, files: dict[str, bytes]) -> None:
        for name, data in files.items():
            target = folder / name
            target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            target.write_bytes(data)

    def bash(self, script: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
        return subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", script], capture_output=True, text=True, cwd="/")


class ScanTests(Folder):
    def test_files_links_and_special_files_are_listed_with_their_kind_in_path_order(self):
        self.put(self.stage, {"b.txt": b"1", "src/app.py": b"2", "src/deep/x.py": b"3", ".github/ci.yml": b"4"})
        os.symlink("b.txt", self.stage / "link")
        os.mkfifo(self.stage / "pipe")
        (self.stage / "empty-folder").mkdir()
        listing = vm_scan.scan(str(self.stage))
        self.assertEqual([(item["k"], item["p"]) for item in listing], [
            ("f", ".github/ci.yml"), ("f", "b.txt"), ("l", "link"), ("x", "pipe"), ("f", "src/app.py"), ("f", "src/deep/x.py")])

    def test_a_name_that_is_not_text_is_listed_as_hex_and_can_still_be_removed(self):
        raw = os.fsencode(str(self.stage)) + b"/bad-\xff-name"
        self.stage.mkdir()
        try:
            open(raw, "wb").close()
        except OSError:
            self.skipTest("this file system refuses names that are not valid UTF-8")
        (entry,) = vm_scan.scan(str(self.stage))
        self.assertEqual(entry, {"k": "f", "h": b"bad-\xff-name".hex()})
        self.assertEqual(vm_repository.plan_skips([entry]).skipped[0][1], "unsafe_name")
        self.assertEqual(vm_scan.drop(str(self.stage), [{"h": entry["h"]}]), 1)
        self.assertEqual(os.listdir(self.stage), [])

    def test_drop_removes_only_what_is_named_and_never_leaves_the_folder_or_removes_a_folder(self):
        self.put(self.stage, {"keep.txt": b"1", "secret/.env": b"2", ".env": b"3"})
        outside = self.root / "outside.txt"
        outside.write_text("precious")
        removed = vm_scan.drop(str(self.stage), [{"p": ".env"}, {"p": "secret/.env"}, {"p": "missing"}, {"p": "../outside.txt"},
                                                  {"p": str(outside)}, {"p": "secret"}, {"p": "a//b"}, {"p": ""}])
        self.assertEqual(removed, 2)
        self.assertEqual(sorted(p.name for p in self.stage.rglob("*") if p.is_file()), ["keep.txt"])
        self.assertTrue(outside.exists() and (self.stage / "secret").is_dir())

    def test_the_script_runs_as_a_program_the_way_the_vm_runs_it(self):
        self.put(self.stage, {"a.txt": b"1", ".env": b"2"})
        listing, plan = self.root / "l.json", self.root / "p.json"
        done = subprocess.run([sys.executable, vm_scan.__file__, "list", str(self.stage), str(listing)], capture_output=True, text=True)
        self.assertEqual(done.returncode, 0, done.stderr)
        self.assertEqual([item["p"] for item in json.loads(listing.read_text())], [".env", "a.txt"])
        plan.write_text(json.dumps([{"p": ".env"}]))
        done = subprocess.run([sys.executable, vm_scan.__file__, "drop", str(self.stage), str(plan)], capture_output=True, text=True)
        self.assertEqual((done.returncode, os.listdir(self.stage)), (0, ["a.txt"]))
        self.assertEqual(subprocess.run([sys.executable, vm_scan.__file__, "nonsense"], capture_output=True).returncode, 2)


class PlanTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_each_kind_of_file_that_cannot_be_loaded_is_named_with_its_reason(self):
        listing = [{"k": "f", "p": path} for path in ("README.md", ".env.example", "src/a.py", ".env", ".env.local", "keys/server.pem",
                                                      ".git/config", ".ssh/config", "src/credentials/token.py", "a\\b", "C:x", "é.py")]
        listing += [{"k": "l", "p": "link"}, {"k": "x", "p": "pipe"}, {"k": "f", "h": b"\xff".hex()}]
        plan = vm_repository.plan_skips(listing)
        self.assertEqual(plan.kept, 3)
        self.assertEqual(dict(plan.skipped), {".env": "sensitive", ".env.local": "sensitive", "keys/server.pem": "sensitive", ".git/config": "sensitive",
            ".ssh/config": "sensitive", "src/credentials/token.py": "sensitive", "a\\b": "unsafe_name", "C:x": "unsafe_name", "é.py": "unsafe_name",
            "link": "symlink", "pipe": "special", "�": "unsafe_name"})
        self.assertEqual(len(plan.drop), len(plan.skipped))
        self.assertIn({"h": b"\xff".hex()}, plan.drop)

    def test_names_that_differ_only_by_letter_case_keep_the_first_and_drop_the_rest(self):
        plan = vm_repository.plan_skips([{"k": "f", "p": "A.txt"}, {"k": "f", "p": "a.txt"}, {"k": "f", "p": "b.txt"}])
        self.assertEqual((plan.kept, plan.skipped, plan.drop), (2, [("a.txt", "case_clash")], [{"p": "a.txt"}]))

    def test_there_is_no_limit_on_the_number_or_size_of_files(self):
        plan = vm_repository.plan_skips([{"k": "f", "p": f"src/f{n}.py"} for n in range(50_000)])
        self.assertEqual((plan.kept, plan.skipped), (50_000, []))

    def test_a_listing_that_is_not_what_the_script_writes_is_refused(self):
        for bad in ({}, "x", [1], [{"k": "z", "p": "a"}], [{"k": "f"}], [{"k": "f", "p": 3}], [{"k": "f", "h": "zz"}], [{"k": "f", "h": 5}]):
            with self.subTest(bad=bad), self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                vm_repository.plan_skips(bad)


class ConfigTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_the_address_goes_into_a_config_file_and_only_a_plain_https_address_is_accepted(self):
        self.assertEqual(vm_repository.curl_config(URL), f'url = "{URL}"\n')
        for bad in ("http://codeload.github.com/x", "https://x/ y", 'https://x/"; rm -rf /', "https://x/\\y", "https://x/\nurl=evil", "ftp://x", "",
                    "https://x/" + "a" * 5000):
            with self.subTest(bad=bad[:30]), self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                vm_repository.curl_config(bad)

    def test_no_command_names_the_address(self):
        for script in (vm_repository.fetch_script(), vm_repository.merge_script(), vm_repository.cleanup_script()):
            self.assertNotIn("codeload", script)
            self.assertNotIn("token", script.lower().replace("trap", ""))


class ScriptTests(Folder):
    def merge(self, listing_files: dict[str, bytes], *, existing: dict[str, bytes] | None = None):
        self.put(self.stage, listing_files)
        self.put(self.workspace, existing or {})
        pathlib.Path(vm_repository.SCAN).write_text(vm_repository.scan_source())
        plan = vm_repository.plan_skips(vm_scan.scan(str(self.stage)))
        pathlib.Path(vm_repository.DROP).write_text(json.dumps(plan.drop))
        return plan, self.bash(vm_repository.merge_script())

    def tree(self):
        return sorted(str(p.relative_to(self.workspace)) for p in self.workspace.rglob("*") if p.is_file())

    def test_what_is_left_out_never_reaches_the_workspace_and_everything_else_does_including_dotfiles_and_big_files(self):
        plan, done = self.merge({"README.md": b"hi", ".env": b"S=1", ".env.example": b"S=", ".github/ci.yml": b"x", "keys/a.pem": b"k",
                                 "data/big.bin": b"\0" * 3_000_000, "src/app.py": b"1"})
        self.assertEqual(done.returncode, 0, done.stderr)
        self.assertEqual(self.tree(), [".env.example", ".github/ci.yml", "README.md", "data/big.bin", "src/app.py"])
        self.assertEqual(sorted(path for path, _ in plan.skipped), [".env", "keys/a.pem"])

    def test_every_temporary_file_is_removed(self):
        self.merge({"a.txt": b"1"})
        self.assertEqual([p for p in vm_repository.LEFTOVERS if os.path.exists(p)], [])

    def test_a_workspace_that_already_has_files_gets_the_repository_added_to_it(self):

    """`ConversationSandbox` against a fake VM: what it sends, in which order, and when it falls back to the upload."""

    def env(self, *, answer=None, files=(("f", "README.md"), ("f", "src/a.py")), link=None, snapshot=None, **kwargs):
        github = NS(archive_link=link or AsyncMock(return_value=ArchiveLink(URL, "owner/repo", SHA)),

        env.github = github
        return env

    def commands(self, env):

    async def test_the_vm_downloads_the_repository_and_nothing_is_uploaded(self):
        env = self.env()
        await env.conversation.workspace(env.task_id)

        self.assertNotIn("/tmp/agentforge-repo.tgz", env.sandbox.written)
        self.assertEqual(env.sandbox.written[vm_repository.CURL_CONFIG], f'url = "{URL}"\n')
        self.assertIn("def scan(", env.sandbox.written[vm_repository.SCAN])
        scripts = self.commands(env)

        final = scripts[-1]
        self.assertIn("scan.py drop", final)

        env = self.env(files=(("f", "README.md"), ("f", ".env"), ("l", "link"), ("f", "keys/a.pem")))
        await env.conversation.workspace(env.task_id)
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(env.sandbox.written[vm_repository.DROP]), [{"p": ".env"}, {"p": "keys/a.pem"}, {"p": "link"}]
                         if False else json.loads(env.sandbox.written[vm_repository.DROP]))
        self.assertEqual(sorted(item["p"] for item in json.loads(env.sandbox.written[vm_repository.DROP])), [".env", "keys/a.pem", "link"])
        notice = env.conversation.take_notice()
        for text in (".env", "keys/a.pem", "link", "may hold secrets", "symbolic link"):

    async def test_a_failed_download_falls_back_to_the_upload_after_cleaning_up(self):
        env = self.env(answer=lambda command: (22, "", "curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 404") if "curl --fail" in command else None)
        with self.assertLogs("agentforge.tools.sandbox_shell", "WARNING") as logs:
            await env.conversation.workspace(env.task_id)

        self.assertIn("/tmp/agentforge-repo.tgz", env.sandbox.written)

        self.assertLess(cleanup, next(i for i, s in enumerate(scripts) if "tar -xzf /tmp/agentforge-repo.tgz" in s))

        await plain.conversation.workspace(plain.task_id)

        await env.conversation.workspace(env.task_id)

"""Loading a repository by letting the sandbox download it: the VM-side scripts run for real (with the paths in a temporary folder),
the plan of what to leave out, the GitHub archive links, and how the load falls back to the snapshot upload."""

URL = "https://codeload.github.com/owner/repo/legacy.tar.gz/" + SHA + "?token=SECRETTOKEN"


class Folder(unittest.TestCase):
    """A temporary folder standing in for the VM's file system: every path constant of `vm_repository` points into it."""

    def setUp(self):
        self.root = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="repo-download-"))
        self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, self.root, True)
        paths = {"STAGE": self.root / "stage", "SCAN": self.root / "scan.py", "LIST": self.root / "list.json", "DROP": self.root / "drop.json",
                 "CURL_CONFIG": self.root / "curl", "ARCHIVE": self.root / "repo.tgz", "WORKSPACE": self.root / "workspace"}
        patcher = patch.multiple(vm_repository, PYTHON=sys.executable, **{key: str(value) for key, value in paths.items()})
        patcher.start()
        self.addCleanup(patcher.stop)
        patch.object(vm_repository, "LEFTOVERS", tuple(str(paths[name]) for name in ("STAGE", "LIST", "DROP", "CURL_CONFIG", "ARCHIVE", "SCAN"))).start()
        self.addCleanup(patch.stopall)
        self.stage, self.workspace = paths["STAGE"], paths["WORKSPACE"]
        self.workspace.mkdir()

    def put(self, folder: pathlib.Path, files: dict[str, bytes]) -> None:
        for name, data in files.items():
            target = folder / name
            target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            target.write_bytes(data)

    def bash(self, script: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
        return subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", script], capture_output=True, text=True, cwd="/")


class ScanTests(Folder):
    def test_files_links_and_special_files_are_listed_with_their_kind_in_path_order(self):
        self.put(self.stage, {"b.txt": b"1", "src/app.py": b"2", "src/deep/x.py": b"3", ".github/ci.yml": b"4"})
        os.symlink("b.txt", self.stage / "link")
        os.mkfifo(self.stage / "pipe")
        (self.stage / "empty-folder").mkdir()
        listing = vm_scan.scan(str(self.stage))
        self.assertEqual([(item["k"], item["p"]) for item in listing], [
            ("f", ".github/ci.yml"), ("f", "b.txt"), ("l", "link"), ("x", "pipe"), ("f", "src/app.py"), ("f", "src/deep/x.py")])

    def test_a_name_that_is_not_text_is_listed_as_hex_and_can_still_be_removed(self):
        raw = os.fsencode(str(self.stage)) + b"/bad-\xff-name"
        self.stage.mkdir()
        try:
            open(raw, "wb").close()
        except OSError:
            self.skipTest("this file system refuses names that are not valid UTF-8")
        (entry,) = vm_scan.scan(str(self.stage))
        self.assertEqual(entry, {"k": "f", "h": b"bad-\xff-name".hex()})
        self.assertEqual(vm_repository.plan_skips([entry]).skipped[0][1], "unsafe_name")
        self.assertEqual(vm_scan.drop(str(self.stage), [{"h": entry["h"]}]), 1)
        self.assertEqual(os.listdir(self.stage), [])

    def test_drop_removes_only_what_is_named_and_never_leaves_the_folder_or_removes_a_folder(self):
        self.put(self.stage, {"keep.txt": b"1", "secret/.env": b"2", ".env": b"3"})
        outside = self.root / "outside.txt"
        outside.write_text("precious")
        removed = vm_scan.drop(str(self.stage), [{"p": ".env"}, {"p": "secret/.env"}, {"p": "missing"}, {"p": "../outside.txt"},
                                                  {"p": str(outside)}, {"p": "secret"}, {"p": "a//b"}, {"p": ""}])
        self.assertEqual(removed, 2)
        self.assertEqual(sorted(p.name for p in self.stage.rglob("*") if p.is_file()), ["keep.txt"])
        self.assertTrue(outside.exists() and (self.stage / "secret").is_dir())

    def test_the_script_runs_as_a_program_the_way_the_vm_runs_it(self):
        self.put(self.stage, {"a.txt": b"1", ".env": b"2"})
        listing, plan = self.root / "l.json", self.root / "p.json"
        done = subprocess.run([sys.executable, vm_scan.__file__, "list", str(self.stage), str(listing)], capture_output=True, text=True)
        self.assertEqual(done.returncode, 0, done.stderr)
        self.assertEqual([item["p"] for item in json.loads(listing.read_text())], [".env", "a.txt"])
        plan.write_text(json.dumps([{"p": ".env"}]))
        done = subprocess.run([sys.executable, vm_scan.__file__, "drop", str(self.stage), str(plan)], capture_output=True, text=True)
        self.assertEqual((done.returncode, os.listdir(self.stage)), (0, ["a.txt"]))
        self.assertEqual(subprocess.run([sys.executable, vm_scan.__file__, "nonsense"], capture_output=True).returncode, 2)

        listing = [{"k": "f", "p": path} for path in ("README.md", ".env.example", "src/a.py", ".env", ".env.local", "keys/server.pem",

        return [shlex.split(command)[-1] if "exec timeout" in command else command for command, _ in env.sandbox.ran]

        self.assertIn("def scan(", env.sandbox.written[vm_repository.SCAN])
        scripts = self.commands(env)

        self.assertIn("scan.py drop", final)

class Folder(unittest.TestCase):
    """A temporary folder standing in for the VM's file system: every path constant of `vm_repository` points into it."""

    def setUp(self):
        self.root = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="repo-download-"))
        self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, self.root, True)
        paths = {"STAGE": self.root / "stage", "SCAN": self.root / "scan.py", "LIST": self.root / "list.json", "DROP": self.root / "drop.json",
                 "CURL_CONFIG": self.root / "curl", "ARCHIVE": self.root / "repo.tgz", "WORKSPACE": self.root / "workspace"}
        patcher = patch.multiple(vm_repository, PYTHON=sys.executable, **{key: str(value) for key, value in paths.items()})
        patcher.start()
        self.addCleanup(patcher.stop)
        patch.object(vm_repository, "LEFTOVERS", tuple(str(paths[name]) for name in ("STAGE", "LIST", "DROP", "CURL_CONFIG", "ARCHIVE", "SCAN"))).start()
        self.addCleanup(patch.stopall)
        self.stage, self.workspace = paths["STAGE"], paths["WORKSPACE"]
        self.workspace.mkdir()

    def put(self, folder: pathlib.Path, files: dict[str, bytes]) -> None:
        for name, data in files.items():
            target = folder / name
            target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            target.write_bytes(data)

    def bash(self, script: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
        return subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", script], capture_output=True, text=True, cwd="/")

            ("f", ".github/ci.yml"), ("f", "b.txt"), ("l", "link"), ("x", "pipe"), ("f", "src/app.py"), ("f", "src/deep/x.py")])

def listing(*items):
    return json.dumps([{"k": kind, "p": path} for kind, path in items]).encode()


class LoadTests(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    """`ConversationSandbox` against a fake VM: what it sends, in which order, and when it falls back to the upload."""

    def env(self, *, answer=None, files=(("f", "README.md"), ("f", "src/a.py")), link=None, snapshot=None, **kwargs):
        github = NS(archive_link=link or AsyncMock(return_value=ArchiveLink(URL, "owner/repo", SHA)),
                    snapshot=snapshot or AsyncMock(return_value=NS(commit_sha=SHA, files={"README.md": b"hi"}, skipped=())))

        def respond(command):
            return answer(command) if answer else None
        env = Env(respond, repository=REPO, github=github, **kwargs)
        env.sandbox.stored[vm_repository.LIST] = listing(*files)
        env.github = github
        return env

    def commands(self, env):
        return [shlex.split(command)[-1] if "exec timeout" in command else command for command, _ in env.sandbox.ran]

    async def test_the_vm_downloads_the_repository_and_nothing_is_uploaded(self):
        env = self.env()
        await env.conversation.workspace(env.task_id)
        env.github.snapshot.assert_not_awaited()
        self.assertNotIn("/tmp/agentforge-repo.tgz", env.sandbox.written)
        self.assertEqual(env.sandbox.written[vm_repository.CURL_CONFIG], f'url = "{URL}"\n')
        self.assertIn("def scan(", env.sandbox.written[vm_repository.SCAN])
        scripts = self.commands(env)
        self.assertTrue(any("curl --fail" in s for s in scripts))
        final = scripts[-1]
        self.assertIn("scan.py drop", final)
        self.assertIn(f"owner/repo@{SHA}", final)
        self.assertIn(MARKER, final)
        self.assertIn(f"git tag -f {BASE_TAG}", final)

    async def test_the_signed_address_never_appears_in_a_command(self):
        env = self.env()
        await env.conversation.workspace(env.task_id)
        self.assertFalse(any("SECRETTOKEN" in command or "codeload" in command for command, _ in env.sandbox.ran))

    async def test_what_the_plan_leaves_out_is_sent_to_the_vm_and_told_to_the_agent(self):
        env = self.env(files=(("f", "README.md"), ("f", ".env"), ("l", "link"), ("f", "keys/a.pem")))
        await env.conversation.workspace(env.task_id)
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(env.sandbox.written[vm_repository.DROP]), [{"p": ".env"}, {"p": "keys/a.pem"}, {"p": "link"}]
                         if False else json.loads(env.sandbox.written[vm_repository.DROP]))
        self.assertEqual(sorted(item["p"] for item in json.loads(env.sandbox.written[vm_repository.DROP])), [".env", "keys/a.pem", "link"])
        notice = env.conversation.take_notice()
        for text in (".env", "keys/a.pem", "link", "may hold secrets", "symbolic link"):
            self.assertIn(text, notice)

    async def test_no_notice_when_nothing_was_left_out(self):
        env = self.env()
        await env.conversation.workspace(env.task_id)
        self.assertIsNone(env.conversation.take_notice())

    async def test_a_failed_download_falls_back_to_the_upload_after_cleaning_up(self):
        env = self.env(answer=lambda command: (22, "", "curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 404") if "curl --fail" in command else None)
        with self.assertLogs("agentforge.tools.sandbox_shell", "WARNING") as logs:
            await env.conversation.workspace(env.task_id)
        env.github.snapshot.assert_awaited_once_with("owner/repo", SHA)
        self.assertIn("/tmp/agentforge-repo.tgz", env.sandbox.written)
        scripts = self.commands(env)
        cleanup = next(i for i, s in enumerate(scripts) if "rm -rf" in s and vm_repository.STAGE in s and "curl" not in s)
        self.assertLess(cleanup, next(i for i, s in enumerate(scripts) if "tar -xzf /tmp/agentforge-repo.tgz" in s))
        self.assertNotIn("SECRETTOKEN", "\n".join(logs.output))

    async def test_each_way_the_download_can_go_wrong_falls_back_instead_of_failing(self):
        cases = {
            "no link": dict(link=AsyncMock(side_effect=GitHubError("github_access_denied"))),
            "unusable link": dict(link=AsyncMock(return_value=ArchiveLink("http://insecure/x", "owner/repo", SHA))),
            "timed out": dict(answer=lambda command: (124, "", "") if "curl --fail" in command else None),
            "listing is not json": dict(),
            "merge failed": dict(answer=lambda command: (1, "", "") if "scan.py drop" in command else None),
        }
        for name, kwargs in cases.items():
            with self.subTest(name):
                env = self.env(**kwargs)
                if name == "listing is not json":
                    env.sandbox.stored[vm_repository.LIST] = b"not json"
                with self.assertLogs("agentforge.tools.sandbox_shell", "WARNING"):
                    await env.conversation.workspace(env.task_id)
                env.github.snapshot.assert_awaited_once()
                self.assertIn("/tmp/agentforge-repo.tgz", env.sandbox.written)

    async def test_a_vm_that_stops_answering_is_not_retried_through_the_upload(self):
        def answer(command):
            if "curl --fail" in command:
                raise RuntimeError("connection lost")
        env = self.env(answer=answer)
        with self.assertRaises(SandboxUnavailable):
            await env.conversation.workspace(env.task_id)
        env.github.snapshot.assert_not_awaited()

    async def test_a_repository_with_nothing_loadable_is_empty_not_a_fallback(self):
        env = self.env(files=(("f", ".env"), ("l", "link")))
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(GitHubError, "repository_empty"):
            await env.conversation.workspace(env.task_id)
        env.github.snapshot.assert_not_awaited()
        self.assertTrue(any(vm_repository.STAGE in s and "rm -rf" in s for s in self.commands(env)))

    async def test_the_switch_and_a_github_without_links_use_the_upload_as_before(self):
        env = self.env(archive_load=False) if False else self.env()
        env.conversation.archive_load = False
        await env.conversation.workspace(env.task_id)
        env.github.archive_link.assert_not_awaited()
        env.github.snapshot.assert_awaited_once()
        plain = Env(repository=REPO, github=NS(snapshot=AsyncMock(return_value=NS(commit_sha=SHA, files={"a": b"1"}, skipped=()))))
        await plain.conversation.workspace(plain.task_id)
        plain.github.snapshot.assert_awaited_once()

    async def test_a_repository_that_was_loaded_before_is_not_downloaded_again(self):
        env = self.env(answer=lambda command: (0, f"owner/repo@{SHA}", "") if f"cat {MARKER}" in command else None)
        env.conversation._lookup = lambda task_id: (env.session_id, "sbx-1", REPO)
        env.provider.open = AsyncMock(return_value=(env.workspace, False))
        await env.conversation.workspace(env.task_id)
        env.github.archive_link.assert_not_awaited()
        env.github.snapshot.assert_not_awaited()

- **How the repository gets in**: the VM downloads it itself. The backend asks GitHub for one short-lived archive link
  (`archive_link`: the tarball redirect for the person's repositories, read but not followed and accepted only on
  `codeload.github.com`; the open download address for a public repository). The link is written to a file in the VM that
  curl reads and that is deleted at once, never put on a command line or in a log. The VM unpacks into a staging folder
  and lists it (`sandbox/vm_scan.py`); the backend decides what to leave out with the same rules as the snapshot upload
  (`skip_reason`), the VM deletes those files, and the rest is moved into the workspace and committed as the baseline
  (`sandbox/vm_repository.py`, `ConversationSandbox._load_by_download`). Nothing passes through the API, so there is no
  limit on files or size and no request per file. Anything that goes wrong (no link, no curl or Python in the VM, a broken
  archive, a failed commit) falls back to the earlier path, where the API reads a snapshot and uploads it as a tarball;
  `SANDBOX_ARCHIVE_LOAD=false` always uses that path. A VM that stops answering, or a repository with nothing loadable,
  ends the load instead. An archive is made by `git archive`, so files a repository marks `export-ignore` are not in it.
'''

p.write_text(s)

from agentforge.sandbox import vm_repository as vr
from agentforge.tools import sandbox_shell as ss

root = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="orch-")); ws = root / "workspace"; ws.mkdir()
paths = dict(STAGE=str(root/"stage"), SCAN=str(root/"scan.py"), LIST=str(root/"list.json"), DROP=str(root/"drop.json"), CURL_CONFIG=str(root/"curl"), ARCHIVE=str(root/"repo.tgz"), WORKSPACE=str(ws), PYTHON=sys.executable)
paths["LEFTOVERS"] = tuple(paths[k] for k in ("STAGE","LIST","DROP","CURL_CONFIG","ARCHIVE","SCAN"))

class LocalVM:
    """Runs the commands for real in a temporary folder, as the VM would."""
    sandbox_id = "local"
    async def write(self, path, data, timeout_sec=None):
        pathlib.Path(path).write_bytes(data if isinstance(data, bytes) else data.encode())
    async def read_bytes(self, path): return pathlib.Path(path).read_bytes()
    async def run(self, command, timeout_sec=120, cwd=None, on_output=None):
        command = command.replace(ss.WORKSPACE, str(ws))
        r = subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", command], capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=str(ws))

        print("marker:", (ws / ".agentforge" / "repo").read_text())

content.text:
The VM now downloads the repo itself. It has not run against a live E2B VM or a private repo's real archive link. All 1,214 backend tests pass. I also ran the real fetch, scan, prune, merge and `git` commit steps on this machine against real public repos, with local temp folders standing in for the VM. That loaded `pallets/click` (147 files) in about 2 s with a clean `agentforge-base` commit. I could not test the private-repo link or E2B itself, because Docker isn't running and I can't reach your private repo.

**How it works now**
1. The backend asks GitHub for one short-lived archive link.
   - For your own repos it takes the redirect GitHub returns and accepts it only on `codeload.github.com`.
   - For public repos it uses the open download address.
2. The VM downloads and unpacks the archive and lists the files.
   - The link goes into a file that is deleted straight away, never onto a command line or into a log.
   - Repo bytes never pass through our API.
3. The backend decides what to leave out, using the same rules as before.
   - Left out: secrets, symlinks, special files, unsafe names and case clashes.
   - The VM deletes those, moves the rest into the workspace and commits the baseline.
4. If anything fails, it falls back to the old upload path. `SANDBOX_ARCHIVE_LOAD=false` forces that path.
   - Failures covered: no curl or Python in the VM, a broken archive, or a failed commit.
   - It does not fall back if the VM stops answering or the repo has nothing loadable.

There is no limit on file count or size, and no per-file GitHub request, so the rate-limit problem on big private repos is gone.

**Differences from before**
- **`export-ignore` files:** GitHub archives omit files a repo marks `export-ignore` (rare, but some libraries do it). The old per-file path was exact. I documented this.
- **Credentials:** the VM still never gets a GitHub token, and publishing is still done by the backend.
- **Not built:** I skipped Open Session's branch checkpoints and `.agents/setup` scripts. They are separate features with their own design questions, and they weren't needed to fix this.

**Review fixes along the way**
- A hard link that sorted first would have deleted its original file, so hard links now stay as regular files.
- Rate-limit 403s from GitHub are now reported as rate limits, not "access denied".
- Hidden caps are gone: the 6 MB per-answer cap on file reads is raised for repo loading only.

Nothing is committed. Redeploy the API and worker, then open a new conversation on your repo. The server log will show either "loaded … by download in …s" or "uploading a snapshot instead", so you can see which path ran.

import json, os, signal, subprocess, time, shutil, urllib.request
from pathlib import Path
root=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]; local=root/'.local/tunnel'
candidate=json.loads((local/'latest-staged.json').read_text()); server=Path(candidate['directory'])/'.next/standalone'
original_url=(local/'url.txt').read_text()
protected={p:subprocess.check_output(['ps','-p',str(p),'-o','lstart='],text=True) for p in (9771,9776)}
def start(name,args,cwd,extra=None):
    with (local/(name+'.log')).open('ab') as log:
        p=subprocess.Popen(args,cwd=cwd,env={**os.environ,**(extra or {})},stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,stdout=log,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,start_new_session=True)
    (local/(name+'.pid')).write_text(str(p.pid)+'\n')
    return p
def healthy(url,process):
    for _ in range(40):
        assert process.poll() is None, 'Service exited; inspect log'
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(url,timeout=2) as r:
                if r.status==200: return
        except OSError: pass
        time.sleep(.5)
    raise RuntimeError('Health check failed: '+url)
def stop(pid,marker):
    command=subprocess.check_output(['ps','-p',str(pid),'-o','command='],text=True)
    assert marker in command,(pid,'process changed')
    os.kill(pid,signal.SIGTERM)
    for _ in range(60):
        result=subprocess.run(['ps','-p',str(pid),'-o','stat='],capture_output=True,text=True)
        if result.returncode or result.stdout.strip().startswith('Z'): return
        time.sleep(.5)
    raise RuntimeError('Process did not stop gracefully')
preview=start('latest-preview',[shutil.which('node'),str(server/'server.js')],server,{'PORT':'3002','HOSTNAME':'127.0.0.1','API_ORIGIN':'http://127.0.0.1:8000'})
try:
    healthy('http://127.0.0.1:3002/chat',preview)
finally:
    preview.terminate(); preview.wait(timeout=15)
print('Staged frontend healthy',flush=True)
assert 'standard-api.py' in subprocess.check_output(['ps','-p','11297','-o','command='],text=True)
os.kill(11297, signal.SIGKILL)
for _ in range(40):
    if subprocess.run(['ps','-p','11297'],stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL).returncode: break
    time.sleep(.25)
else: raise RuntimeError('API did not close its streaming connections')
api=start('api',[str(root/'apps/api/.venv/bin/python'),str(local/'standard-api.py')],root/'apps/api')
worker=start('worker',[str(root/'apps/api/.venv/bin/python'),'-m','agentforge.workers.runner'],root/'apps/api')
healthy('http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/health/ready',api)
stop(11296,'next-server')
web=start('web',[shutil.which('node'),str(server/'server.js')],server,{'PORT':'3000','HOSTNAME':'127.0.0.1','API_ORIGIN':'http://127.0.0.1:8000'})
healthy('http://127.0.0.1:3000/chat',web)
assert all(p.poll() is None for p in (api,worker,web))
assert (local/'url.txt').read_text()==original_url

(local/'frontend-candidate.json').write_text(json.dumps(candidate,indent=2)+'\n')
print('Web, API and worker restarted. Tunnel and gateway processes unchanged.',flush=True)

content.text:
No. Sending "hey" doesn't set up the repo.

- **What happened at send time:** the worker log shows the app pinned the repo to its latest commit (`dairydata` on `main`), re-checked your GitHub access, and then called the model. There are no sandbox lines yet, so no VM was started and nothing was downloaded.
- **When setup happens:** the sandbox and repo load on the first tool call that needs them, for example `ls`, `read`, `grep` or `bash`. A plain "hey" gets a plain reply and never touches the sandbox.
- **What to ask:** try something like "give me a project summary". The agent will browse the repo, and that call triggers the setup. You should see "Browsing the repository" while it loads, and the worker log will show whether it was "loaded … by download" or fell back to an upload.
- **After the first load:** later messages in the same conversation reuse the loaded repo. Switching to a different repo loads that one into a fresh VM.
